paragraphs: Rabbi Abba bar Mammal. It appears that he is Rabbi Abba without qualification (see there), except that at the end of Chullin it appears that Rabbi Abba answered Rabbi Abba bar Mammal; accurate Talmud editions do not mention Rabbi Abba. (But in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shevuot, chapter 3, halakhah 2: Rabbi Ba, Rabbi Yirmeyah, Rabbi Bon bar Chiyya in Rabbi Abba bar Mammal’s name. Perhaps there too this is a scribal error, for immediately afterward Rabbi Ba is not mentioned.) Rabbi Zeira said, “Throughout Rabbi Abba bar Mammal’s life we found no answer against him; after he died we found an answer” (Jerusalem Talmud, Shevuot, chapter 3, halakhah 4). In Bava Batra 67b: “What is mammal? Rabbi Abba bar Mammal said: the crushing apparatus.” (Rabbah bar Mammal, Bava Metzia 56b; Rabbah bar Mammal and Rav Amram, Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of the first chapter of Bava Metzia; Ravin bar Mammal, Jerusalem Talmud, end of chapter Hazahav—perhaps all are one.) He said in Rav’s name (Bava Batra 38a and 88b; Jerusalem Talmud, first chapter of Makkot: Rabbi Ba bar Mammal, Rav Amram, Rav Mattanah, in Rav’s name). Rabbi Abba in his name (see below); and Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, Rabbi Abba bar Zutra, Rabbi Avina, Rabbi Acha bar Yitzchak, Rabbi Iva. He sat before Rabbi Ammi (Yevamot 105a), asked Rabbi Ammi (Bava Kamma 19a), and objected to Rabbi Ammi (Bava Metzia 36a). He told Rabbi Ammi, “You told us in Rabbi Yehudah Nesia’s name” (Nedarim 21a). Rabbi Ammi sent to him (Bava Batra 59a). Rav Assi says to Rabbi Zeira, “Afterward I asked Rabbi Abba bar Mammal” (Chullin, printed here as קכ"ט יא). Rabbi Bon bar Chiyya in his name (see below); Rabbi Bon bar Bisna in his name; he asked Rabbi Hoshaya the elder (Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Keitzad Haregel); Rabbi Zevida in his name. Rabbi Zeira bar Mammal—perhaps his brother. Rabbi Zeira told him (Chullin 141a) and disagreed with him (Sukkah, printed here as כ א ב), Mo'ed Katan 4b; Ze'ira before him (Shevi'it, chapter 2), and in his name (Ma'aser Sheni, first chapter, halakhah 2); Rabbi Chizkiyah in his name. He objected to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba (Bava Kamma 19a, 35b, 106b; Shevuot 40b). He asked Rabbi Yehudah Nesia (Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Keitzad Haregel). Rabbi Yochanan in Rabbi Abba bar Mammal’s name (so Yuchasin writes; I did not find it). Rabbi Abba bar Mammal said, “Have they not heard what Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi’s name?”, Zevachim 99b. Rabbi Yirmeyah in his name (see below). Rabbi Yitzchak Atishaya recited a teaching to him (see below). Rabbi Mattanah (see below), and Rabbi Amram (see below). He said in Rav’s name (see above); he asked before Rav (Jerusalem Talmud, Pe'ah, last chapter). He asked before Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak, who answered him. Rabbi Abba bar Mammal stood with Rabbi Yirmeyah and told Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak, “See how what you adduce as proof flies in the air!” Rabbi Ze'ira brought Rabbi Yitzchak Atishaya, who recited it to him (Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter 3 of Sotah).
